title: Dexter Gordon and the bebop era
summary: Harris says Dexter Gordon was close to but not quite bebop, and places the great saxophonists.

blocks.x: How was that relationship, and how was…
And how did you like his harmonic sense of movement and things, how was…
Well, his is slightly different, it’s not Bird, but it’s slightly different. He was around a long time, you know, Dexter was around at the beginning of Bird.

You know. Dexter is a little slightly different than Bird. Well, see Bird was like the new era. I call him the, I was part of the renaissance, I call it the renaissance period. The most musical period in the music was Bird and Bud and Dizzy Gillespie and Fats Navarro, you know they the masters.
So Dexter was between now and sometime…
He was during that period but he wasn’t quite what I would call bebopper, it was good though, you know. These cats was different, you know.
And Webster, so you’re saying, would you say Ben Webster…
Coleman Hawkins. Graves:…did he ever say ilk…

Yeah, Coleman Hawkins. Well, well, no, no, Dexter might be a little in between. Here’s Coleman Hawkins, Ben Webster and…other people. They’re sort of here, Dexter might have been a little notch on his own the way he played. There were, we had Wardell Gray, we had Gene Ammons, we had Yusef Lateef, all these guys, these cats, they played
